properties.title: CoRe-WM: Conditioned Response-State World Modeling for Longitudinal Treatment-Response Prediction in Breast DCE-MRI
properties.bibliographic_check: Title and byline checked against supplied physical-page-1 text and its supplied visual review notes; no external bibliographic verification.

properties.hash_provenance: Supplied source record; not recomputed in this response.
properties.source_access: All ten pages of extracted text and all ten page-image review notes supplied. Original PDF bytes and page images were not directly available to this synthesis pass.
properties.publication_caution: IEEE Transactions on Medical Imaging running headers do not independently establish journal acceptance or peer review.
properties.supplements: No separate supplements supplied or identified in the supplied paper; references end on page 10.

properties.design: Retrospective secondary analysis of actual I-SPY2 and I-SPY1 clinical-trial imaging and clinical data.
properties.investigation: Outcome-label-free next-visit representation pretraining followed by frozen-state pCR prediction, internal validation, source-only cross-cohort transfer, calibration, ablations, permutation tests, and response-state probes.

membership_assessment.classification: Core healthcare world model at implementation stage; representation-evaluated identity tier.
membership_assessment.basis: An implemented learned transition advances a retained visit-state history over breast-treatment visit index. Reported evaluations demonstrate representation and endpoint quality, not future-state forecast fidelity.
not_established: Evaluated next-visit latent or geometry forecasting

properties.independence: One reported study with dependent folds, prefixes, probes, and ablations. These are not independent clinical validations.

properties.name: Conditioned Response-state World Modeling
properties.configuration_scope: Paper-described full FRS+IRG configuration; five fold-specific trained checkpoints, not one externally inspected weight file.
properties.encoder: Four-stage 3-D residual CNN with channels 16, 32, 64, 128; global pooling and layer normalization; image and geometry embeddings combined additively.
properties.transition: Three conditioned causal Transformer blocks, four attention heads, feed-forward dimension 512, dropout 0.1; additive conditioning plus FiLM.
properties.response_path: A smaller conditioned Transformer processes lesion geometry history and supplies response states, geometry and response heads, and an additive latent correction.
properties.time_distinction: Epochs, EMA updates, and optimization steps are not clinical visits.
properties.code_status: Announced for release upon publication; no repository URL supplied.

properties.configuration: Image-only JEPA; no profile, treatment, explicit geometry, FRS, or IRG.
properties.evaluation_scope: T0–T1 frozen-readout pCR discrimination on the same five I-SPY2 folds.

properties.configuration: Image-only JEPA plus HR, HER2, MammaPrint, and age.
Profile and treatment conditioning plus explicit ROI geometry.
Profile, treatment, geometry, and factorized response state; before addition of IRG.

properties.flow: Per-visit MRI preprocessing and geometry extraction → image/geometry encoders and observed-prefix histories → conditioned image and response-state transitions → frozen response-prefix features → class-balanced logistic pCR readout.
properties.downstream_readout: One class-balanced logistic regression pooled across patients and decision points; validation-selected penalty and regularization.
properties.calibration_variant: Fold-specific validation-fitted Platt scaling for the internal calibration analysis; not automatically assigned to every native or external result.
properties.composition_pattern: Serial preprocessing/representation/readout pipeline with parallel coupled imaging and geometry-response pathways.
properties.clinical_authority: Offline prediction only. Decision curves model referral for review, but no actual referral workflow, treatment-selection policy, or actuation is demonstrated.
properties.module_completeness: Implemented subresponsibilities only; no complete ten-module clinical platform or validated ontology interface conformance is asserted.

properties.population: Patients represented in the I-SPY2 and I-SPY1 neoadjuvant breast cancer imaging cohorts.
properties.purpose: Estimate final pCR after T0, T1, or T2 has actually been observed.
properties.decision_boundary: Potential referral for treatment-adaptation review is analyzed retrospectively, not executed.
properties.unsupported_use: Choosing unassigned regimens, estimating individual treatment effects, autonomous treatment adjustment, or claiming realized patient benefit.

properties.coordinate: Ordered treatment-visit index T0, T1, T2, T3.
properties.encoding: Learned visit-position/temporal embeddings and causal sequence mask.
properties.maximum_context_reported: Four-visit study sequences; pCR evaluation uses up to three observed visits.

properties.persistent_context: Observed ordered latent-state prefix z_0:t carried as Transformer context.
properties.response_state: 64-dimensional predicted response state from observed lesion-descriptor prefix.
properties.update: Recompute/extend the prefix from newly observed actual visits while retaining frozen model parameters.
properties.belief_distribution: No posterior/filter distribution is specified by this architecture.
properties.indexing_issue: Section III-A, Section III-F, and Figure 1 use inconsistent response-state indexing; exact baseline/readout feature construction requires clarification.

properties.name: Assigned therapy arm/family
properties.representation: Categorical learned embeddings included with baseline clinical profile in c=(b,a).
properties.actual_evaluation_use: Recorded assigned context and diagnostic permutations; no executable therapy command.
properties.time_semantics: Shared assigned-treatment context across visits, combined with visit embeddings.
properties.support: Limited treatment-subtype overlap acknowledged; no operational support checker reported.
properties.non_actions: Age, receptor status, and MammaPrint are baseline covariates, not clinical actions.

properties.operator: z-hat_(t+1)=T_theta(z_0:t,c), with a parallel geometry-response pathway and additive correction.
properties.structural_prior: Treatment response is represented primarily through lesion morphology; explicit geometry pathway and imaging-derived response guidance.
properties.training_targets: EMA next-visit image-plus-geometry latent; next geometry and observed response summaries.
properties.training_feedback: Observed prefixes supply each one-step successor training example; summing T−1 losses does not establish a recursive k-step loss.
properties.reported_forecast_evaluation: No held-out next-state/geometry forecast fidelity or horizon curve reported.
properties.causal_terminology: Causal Transformer denotes attention masking, not causal treatment identification.

properties.responsibility: M1 subresponsibility: implemented imaging preprocessing and descriptor extraction.
properties.inputs: DCE-MRI phases and released lesion masks.
properties.outputs: Eight-channel 32×96×96 voxel volumes centered on T0 lesion; nine geometry descriptors.
properties.details: Robust per-visit normalization; enhancement-based localization when a compatible released mask is unavailable.
properties.limits: No complete availability-time/provenance service or validated interface contract; physical voxel spacing and fallback frequency not reported.

properties.responsibility: M2 subresponsibility: image and geometry encoding with additive fusion.
properties.inputs: Per-visit eight-channel MRI and nine geometry features.
properties.training: Online/EMA target encoders; latent prediction, SIGReg, and response guidance.
properties.foundation_reuse: No named pretrained foundation encoder reported for CoRe-WM; ImageNet MAE initialization belongs to a comparator.

properties.responsibility: M3 subresponsibility: retain observed visit context and frozen response-state prefixes.
properties.limits: Not an explicit probabilistic belief filter; new-prefix updating is not weight adaptation.

properties.responsibility: M4 subresponsibility: encode assigned treatment categories.
properties.inputs: Assigned treatment arm/family and separately identified baseline clinical covariates.
properties.outputs: Condition embeddings for additive shifts and FiLM.
properties.limits: No full action validation, dosing/schedule, bundle, contraindication, or support service.

properties.responsibility: M5 subresponsibility: learned next-visit image-latent and factorized-response transitions.
properties.inputs: Observed state/descriptor prefixes and clinical/treatment/visit context.
properties.outputs: Next-latent point prediction, predicted response state, geometry estimate, response vector, and response score.
properties.limits: Implementation documented through executed pretraining; successful future-state prediction not evaluated separately.

properties.additional_analysis: Validation-fitted Platt calibration and retrospective decision curves.
properties.causal_subrole: Not implemented by the documented predictive readout.

properties.name: I-SPY 2 breast dynamic contrast enhanced MRI trial (ISPY2)
properties.data_kind: Actual de-identified clinical-trial imaging and clinical data.
properties.access: Described as publicly available; access conditions were not independently checked.

properties.name: I-SPY 1/ACRIN 6657 DCE-MRI data and segmentations
properties.release_description: 2016 resource cited in reference [22]; exact downloaded snapshot not reported.
properties.data_kind: Actual de-identified clinical-trial imaging and clinical data.

properties.split: Five patient-disjoint folds stratified by pCR and HR/HER2 subtype.
properties.count_caution: Approximate fold counts are copied as reported, not summed as exact counts.

properties.role: Distinct trial cohort evaluated without target-outcome fitting or threshold selection.

properties.task: Probe observed T0-to-T2 volume shrinkage from frozen T0-to-T2 state change.

properties.tasks: Final-pCR classification at observed prefixes, plus representation diagnostics.
properties.internal: Common patient-level folds and seed across methods; validation-selected hyperparameters, checkpoints, logistic penalty, and Youden thresholds.
properties.external: Five source-fold predictions averaged per I-SPY1 patient; mean source-validation threshold; no target-outcome fitting.
properties.uncertainty: Fold mean±SD for native internal results; patient bootstrap intervals for specified pooled/external analyses.

properties.endpoint: Final pCR after actual observed prefixes.

properties.aggregation: Mean of five source-fold probabilities per external patient.
properties.result_boundary: External pCR discrimination declines with additional observed visits.

properties.method: Platt calibrator fitted on each validation partition and applied to the corresponding held-out test partition.
properties.aggregation: Pooled calibrated OOF probabilities; distinct from native arithmetic fold means.
properties.calibration_target: Final-pCR event probabilities at observed prefixes, not latent-state or joint-trajectory coverage.

properties.scope_limit: Internal retrospective event-probability calibration after validation-only recalibration; no clinical acceptance threshold or external calibration result.

properties.configurations: Six cumulative configurations, including full CoRe-WM.
properties.controls: Same folds, seed, pretraining budget, and frozen-readout protocol.
properties.limits: One addition order; not a factorial or multiseed component-effect study.

properties.protocol: Keep MRI latents, geometry, fold checkpoints, and native FLR fixed; permute treatment within HR/HER2 strata, profile within treatment families, or joint context globally.
properties.endpoint: pCR AUROC, not future-state or treatment-effect error.
properties.interpretation: Tests model reliance on recorded context. No same-origin clinically specified alternative-regimen consequence comparison or causal identification.

properties.protocol: Outcome-free ridge probe of frozen T0-to-T2 state change; regularization selected on validation partition and predictions restricted to held-out partition.
properties.boundary: T2 contributes to the state update. This is representation grounding for an observed interval, not a T0-only forecast of unseen T2.
properties.target_dependence: Lesion-volume changes already contribute to IRG pretraining.

properties.aggregation_issue: Table IV labels values pooled OOF but its overall row closely tracks Table I fold means; precise native-prediction aggregation requires clarification.
properties.interpretation: Subgroup evaluation exists; nonsignificant pairwise differences do not establish equivalence or fairness.

properties.result: T0–T2 curve reportedly exceeds both default strategies at non-pCR thresholds 0.22–0.75.
properties.clinical_boundary: Retrospective decision-curve analysis; no model-coupled treatment optimizer, actual review workflow, or measured consequence of therapy changes.

criteria_met: The paper identifies the clinical source collections and their cited releases.
The operational preprocessing description identifies MRI-derived channels, lesion-mask sources, localization fallback, per-visit normalization, cropping/padding, and geometry extraction.
criteria_missing: Measurement-level retention of source identifiers and transformation lineage is not documented.
Actual acquisition and information-availability timestamps are not documented as retained.
Physical measurement units, voxel spacing, and complete unit/conversion provenance are not reported.
assertions.rationale: Dataset identity and specified transformations establish part of the provenance responsibility, but not the complete variable-level contract. This automated assessment uses the supplied full text and documented page-image review notes; it does not claim a fresh inspection of PDF bytes or images.

scope.time_horizon: Treatment visits T0–T3; elapsed durations not reported

assertions.rationale: The paper specifies ordered treatment visits and learned visit-position embeddings, but does not establish retention or reversible availability of actual recorded acquisition times. Visit indexing is not native timestamp retention. Irreversible timestamp deletion is also not established.

Observed-prefix restrictions and temporal attention masking are described, but acquisition time is not distinguished from the time MRI-derived measurements, masks, or clinical variables became usable. No release-latency audit is reported. This reporting gap does not establish use of prematurely available information.

The binary lesion-region channel is an anatomical ROI mask, and the causal Transformer mask restricts attention. Neither establishes measured/missing/invalid status for observations. Handling of missing visits, unavailable clinical covariates, or invalid measurements is insufficiently reported.

The retained visit history and visit-position embeddings do not establish per-variable elapsed time since true observation. Carry-forward/asynchronous measurement semantics and freshness updates are not described sufficiently to establish presence, absence, or a specific inapplicability dependency.

The executed transition uses learned visit-position embeddings. Actual elapsed intervals, native event times, and continuous-time integration affecting predictions are not reported. The source also does not explicitly establish the absent criterion of assuming uniform spacing while ignoring known unequal intervals. Neither irregular-time handling nor uniform clinical cadence is inferred.

The model predicts visit states conditional on observed histories and assigned context, but no model or rule is reported for when, whether, or why MRI examinations occur conditional on state or acquisition context. Scheduled trial visits and temporal embeddings alone do not establish observation-process modeling. An explicit ignorable-sampling assumption is not supplied either.

No target-specific temporal witness-preservation audit is reported across sampled values, update/validity patterns, native timestamps, or external acquisition channels. MRI phase selection and voxel cropping are not such an audit. No observation-clock regime is assigned.

Adaptive phase selection, eight-channel construction, robust intensity normalization, and standardized voxel-array dimensions are described. These preprocessing steps do not sufficiently document source-specific units, terminology, and measurement definitions mapped to a declared semantic target schema with traceable conversions. Successful cross-cohort prediction does not establish that contract.

criteria_met: Five disjoint patient-level folds are reported, with a common manifest across compared methods.
Hyperparameters, checkpoints, readout regularization, and classification thresholds are validation-selected.
Platt calibrators are fitted on validation patients and applied to the corresponding held-out test patients.
Causal attention and observed-prefix evaluation restrict the predictor to available visits; T3 is identified as a pretraining target rather than a pCR-predictor input.
criteria_missing: A complete audit explicitly excluding held-out trajectories from every pretraining operation is not reported.
Training-only fitting of all treatment-category response-standardization and target-construction statistics is not explicitly documented.
Complete acquisition-versus-availability-time, site/time-overlap, and preprocessing-fit audits are not reported.
assertions.rationale: Several concrete split, selection, calibration, and temporal-input controls are implemented. They do not establish the feature's complete leakage-audit criterion. Outcome-free pretraining is not itself evidence of partition isolation. No leakage violation is inferred.

criteria_met: The source-fold models, pCR readouts, and operating thresholds are reported as fitted using I-SPY2 only.
External probabilities are averaged across source-fold models, and the mean source-validation threshold is transferred without target-outcome fitting or selection.
criteria_missing: A formal participant-overlap audit between the trial resources is not reported.
Complete source-only fitting and transfer details for every preprocessing and response-target construction statistic are not explicitly audited.
Information-release timing and relevant site/time boundaries are not fully documented.
assertions.rationale: The external protocol provides specific protection against target-outcome adaptation, supporting a separate partial assessment. It does not automatically establish a complete provenance and leakage audit for the composed pipeline.

Public de-identified multicenter trial resources are described, but no site-local training/query protocol or exchanged federated artifacts are reported. Multicenter data and de-identification do not establish federation. The source does not meet the explicit negative criterion involving centrally pooled identifiable records.

criteria_met: A four-stage 3-D residual network operationally maps specified MRI volumes to appearance features.
A geometry MLP maps nine lesion descriptors into the shared latent space, and the image and geometry encodings are added.
The resulting 192-dimensional visit representation supplies the history consumed by the conditioned transition.
assertions.rationale: The observation-to-representation mapping and executed training configuration are documented. This establishes encoder implementation, not an isolated test of encoder optimality or successful future-state prediction. Comparator-specific ImageNet initialization is not attributed to this encoder.

No named externally pretrained checkpoint is reported as supplying CoRe-WM encoder parameters or features. ImageNet masked-autoencoder initialization belongs to the ViT comparator. CoRe-WM's own self-supervised pretraining and EMA target encoder do not establish foundation-model reuse. Explicit from-scratch initialization is not sufficiently stated to code absence.

scope.time_horizon: One successor visit per observed-prefix training example

criteria_met: The transition predicts a next-visit latent from an observed state prefix and clinical/treatment conditions.
The training target is the separate EMA encoder's next-visit image-plus-geometry representation.
Layer-normalized latent MSE is an explicit term in the executed joint pretraining objective.
assertions.rationale: This is an implemented predictive-latent objective, not merely a latent bottleneck or a cited JEPA architecture. Auxiliary descriptor/response losses coexist with it. Downstream pCR and observed-interval probe results do not establish held-out successor-state forecasting accuracy, so implementation is not promoted to forecast evaluation.

criteria_met: A separate stop-gradient target encoder is updated by EMA, with reported momentum 0.996.
The executed pretraining loss includes SIGReg distributional regularization, with reported weight 0.09, explicitly intended to keep latent representations well spread.
assertions.rationale: The source specifies operational anti-collapse mechanisms beyond an algorithm name. Presence denotes their implemented inclusion, not proof that EMA guarantees non-collapse or that a dedicated collapse diagnostic or ablation succeeded.

value.absence_scope: MRI observation reconstruction in the image-encoding/JEPA pathway

assertions.rationale: The inspected image pathway predicts EMA target latents rather than reconstructing MRI observations. Its declared objective uses latent prediction and distribution regularization, alongside separate geometry/response prediction tasks. The absence assessment is restricted to MRI observation reconstruction; it does not deny the auxiliary numerical prediction losses or claim that the complete model lacks observed-target supervision.

criteria_met: MRI appearance and structured clinical information enter a combined computational model.
Image and lesion-descriptor embeddings are combined additively; clinical-profile and assigned-treatment embeddings interact with temporal features through additive conditioning and FiLM.
assertions.rationale: The operational combination of imaging and non-imaging clinical information supports multimodal fusion. Lesion geometry is derived from MRI, so its additive combination with appearance, or the eight MRI channels alone, is not treated as sufficient evidence of independently acquired modalities. This assertion establishes the implemented fusion mechanism, not missing-modality robustness or its isolated effectiveness.

The described additive fusion and FiLM pathways do not sufficiently report modality-availability masks, quality or recency weighting, or behavior when imaging or clinical inputs are missing. Enhancement-based localization when a compatible lesion mask is unavailable is a preprocessing fallback, not demonstrated availability-aware fusion. The incomplete missing-input specification does not justify declaring this feature absent.

scope.time_horizon: Observed treatment-visit prefix T0 through the current visit

criteria_met: Defined visit latents and lesion-descriptor histories are retained as ordered prefixes.
The transition consumes the retained prefix to produce a next-visit latent and response state.
Frozen response-state prefixes also feed subsequent pCR readout.
assertions.rationale: Persistence is supplied by explicitly retained sequence context rather than an isolated embedding or a claimed recurrent posterior. Executed pretraining and downstream use document implementation; they do not establish held-out successor-state prediction accuracy.

Scoped architectural absence follows from the documented point-vector formulation: image and geometry encoders produce a latent vector, conditioned Transformers produce point predictions, and training matches these predictions to encoded targets. The maintained state has no posterior or filtering-distribution parameterization in the specified algorithm. SIGReg regularizes the distribution of representations across samples; it is not a conditional belief over an individual patient's hidden state. Logistic pCR probabilities, fold variation, and bootstrap intervals likewise do not turn this state into a belief distribution.

The documented algorithm encodes actual visits into an observed prefix and predicts the next latent from that prefix. It does not provide a distinct operation that corrects a propagated prior state using an arriving observation. The named latent correction adds a geometry-response prediction to the image-path prediction; it is not observation-conditioned filtering correction. This absence is restricted to the specified CoRe-WM algorithm and does not negate its ability to extend context with new visits.

scope.time_horizon: Successively observed T0, T0–T1, and T0–T2 prefixes

criteria_met: New actual patient visits extend the individual state context at inference.
The pretrained representation model remains frozen while updated prefixes produce revised pCR estimates.
Results are reported at successive observed prefixes in held-out clinical patients.
assertions.rationale: This satisfies the broad arriving-evidence update criterion through prefix extension and recomputation, not through a propagate–correct filter. Internal fold-mean pCR AUROC is 0.7337, 0.7545, and 0.7620 at the three prefixes. No assimilation-specific accuracy test or acceptance criterion is reported. The evaluation is retrospective sequential use, not live online deployment.

scope.time_horizon: Successively observed T0, T0–T1, and T0–T2 prefixes

criteria_met: Transferred frozen source models incorporate additional actual visits in individual observed prefixes.
External pCR predictions are reported separately at each prefix without target-outcome fitting.
assertions.rationale: Arriving-evidence incorporation is exercised externally, but its existence must not be conflated with benefit: external AUROC decreases from 0.7396 to 0.7321 and 0.7082 as visits are added. The paper does not report an assimilation-specific acceptance test. This is not prospective external system use or proof that updating improves predictions under cohort shift.

The reported inference protocol explicitly freezes the pretrained model and fits a pooled population readout, rather than fitting individual patient parameters. Newly observed MRI changes the patient's context and features, not model weights. Source-only external transfer further retains fitted source models and readouts. This establishes absence of per-patient parameter adaptation in the documented use, not absence of individual history conditioning.

criteria_met: The frozen learned response representation supplies a logistic readout for final pCR.
The same frozen representation supplies a separately fitted ridge probe of observed log-volume shrinkage without defining or retraining a new state model.
assertions.rationale: The two typed readouts operate on different summaries of the shared learned state: prefix summaries for pCR in the 808-patient cohort, and T0-to-T2 state change for shrinkage probing in the 791-patient subset. The latter retains a geometric signal already targeted by IRG and includes observed T2; it is not an independent future-state forecast. No general task-reuse acceptance criterion is reported.

scope.time_horizon: Final pCR from the observed T0–T1 prefix

criteria_met: Controlled cumulative configurations alter clinical conditioning, treatment conditioning, geometry, response-state factorization, and response guidance.
The configurations share folds, seed, pretraining budget, and frozen-readout protocol and are compared against the same pCR target.
assertions.rationale: These are relevant representation/variable ablations, so a state-sufficiency assessment is present. Patient profile gives the largest gain, whereas adding treatment after profile has a reported increment of −0.0019±0.0467. Geometry, FRS, and IRG contribute subsequent gains. The result does not prove a sufficient statistic, isolate order-independent component effects, or establish sufficiency for next-state prediction or treatment selection. Ablation configurations remain distinct from the full model.

scope.time_horizon: Final pCR from the observed T0–T2 prefix

criteria_met: Clinical and treatment inputs are perturbed while MRI latents, geometry, model checkpoints, and the native readout are held fixed.
Held-out pCR discrimination quantifies the resulting dependence on conditioning variables.
assertions.rationale: This is a scoped test of which supplied variables contribute to the fitted response representation. Observed-context AUROC is 0.7621±0.0365, versus 0.7329±0.0321 after treatment permutation, 0.6476±0.0210 after clinical-profile permutation, and 0.5951±0.0242 after joint permutation. No sufficiency acceptance criterion is reported. Condition dependence neither proves that all transition determinants are retained nor identifies treatment effects.

scope.time_horizon: Observed visit history through the current treatment visit

criteria_met: The transition explicitly consumes z_0:t rather than only the current image embedding.
The response pathway processes the individual's lesion-descriptor sequence q_0:t.
Causal attention and positional embeddings preserve prefix order, and the readout uses accumulated response-state summaries.
assertions.rationale: Individual observed imaging history affects the inferred response representation through an explicit sequence mechanism. Assigned treatment is shared context rather than a fully specified time-varying action history. This implementation does not by itself prove history-specific personalization beyond generic prognostic priors.

scope.time_horizon: Final pCR from the observed T0–T2 prefix

criteria_met: The analysis contrasts correctly supplied patient clinical context with permuted context while holding the patient's MRI, geometry, checkpoint, and readout fixed.
Clinical-profile permutation within treatment families reduces held-out discrimination, providing a limited analogous individual-context control.
criteria_missing: No matched own-versus-swapped or withheld longitudinal imaging-history test establishes the value of the correct individual's trajectory.
No population-prior or adequately prognostic-stratum-matched control separates individualized trajectory value from receptor-subtype, age, and other generic prognostic information.
Complete partition isolation for all pretraining and response-standardization operations is not explicitly audited.
assertions.rationale: The reported permutations provide a meaningful but limited context-matching diagnostic. They do not complete the feature's beyond-generic-priors criterion: the paper itself identifies molecular profile and age as the dominant signals and acknowledges correlated treatment/subtype structure. Increasing observed-prefix AUROC and probing volume shrinkage do not substitute for the missing personalization controls.

No declared transition memory, constraint, or loss specifically establishes preservation of patient identity or anatomical entities through generated transitions. T0-centered cropping, lesion-morphology supervision, EMA targets, and causal attention have other stated responsibilities and do not alone meet this criterion. No identity-violation evaluation is reported either; therefore neither presence nor absence is established.

criteria_met: The response pathway has documented geometry and imaging-change targets with interpretable lesion-response meaning.
A validation-tuned held-out ridge probe maps frozen state change to observed log-volume shrinkage, and Figure 2d exposes that mapping for inspection.
The probe reports Spearman correlation 0.8623 with 95% CI 0.8347–0.8865 and pooled R² 0.6744 in 791 patients.
criteria_missing: A semantic mapping of the latent state beyond the probed aggregate geometric-response signal is not established.
An operational means for users to inspect individual state variables and their semantic limits is not reported.
assertions.rationale: Interpretability is demonstrated only for a bounded geometric-response aspect, not all latent coordinates or a clinically inspectable state service. Actual T2 contributes to the state update, and volume response already contributes to IRG; the probe is therefore representation grounding rather than unseen-future prediction or independent biomarker discovery.

scope.time_horizon: Short treatment-visit prefixes from four-visit study sequences; downstream pCR inputs extend through T2

criteria_met: Causal Transformer attention retains access to earlier visit states beyond the current supplied state.
A parallel Transformer retains lesion-descriptor history.
Prefix summaries include initial state, prefix mean, recent revision, and cumulative displacement.
assertions.rationale: The specified mechanism is ordered attention context, not an external memory store or recurrent posterior. Its clinical duration and delayed-effect capacity are not reported. The existence of short visit-history memory does not establish useful long-horizon memory.

scope.time_horizon: Next treatment visit under the supplied assigned-regimen context

criteria_met: Assigned therapy a is explicitly distinguished from baseline clinical profile b and imaging state.
The supplied categorical therapy arm/family is encoded and conditions the transition through additive shifts and FiLM.
Condition-permutation experiments establish that the treatment input can be changed computationally.
assertions.rationale: This is an explicit, settable categorical treatment input at implementation stage. Age, receptor status, and MammaPrint remain covariates rather than actions. The assertion does not establish an executable regimen specification, evaluated action-conditioned successor fidelity, causal treatment effects, or clinically supported alternative-regimen comparison.

The source identifies a therapeutic regimen category separately from baseline covariates, so its treatment meaning is recoverable. However, it does not sufficiently report an operational action-role/effect-channel typing representation or a mechanism distinguishing therapeutic, inquiry, acquisition, or other roles. Therapeutic and physiology labels in the existing ActionSpec are reviewer ontology mappings, not evidence that CoRe-WM implements that typing responsibility. A single therapeutic action family is not itself evidence of absence or a reason for blanket inapplicability.
A conditioned causal Transformer predicts the next visit latent from observed prefix states.
Next-imaging latent transitions are learned with outcome-label-free predictive objectives.
Assigned therapy and clinical profile condition next-state prediction; no unassigned-regimen causal claim.
Frozen response states feed a class-balanced logistic pCR readout.
Next-state predictions operate in JEPA image/geometry response representations.
Fold-validation Platt scaling is evaluated on held-out outcome probabilities; this is not trajectory calibration.

Held-out event-probability calibration reports Brier score, ECE and calibration slope/intercept. Evaluation is reported; this annotation does not establish a formal categorical acceptance outcome, so no pass/fail result is inferred.

I-SPY1 transfer and subtype analyses are reported; external AUROC declines with later imaging. Evaluation is reported; this annotation does not establish a formal categorical acceptance outcome, so no pass/fail result is inferred.
Authors state secondary deidentified-data ethics exemption; not regulatory clearance.

capability_assessments.rationale: Core learned health-world dynamics are implemented, so this is not dismissed as merely an unrelated static classifier. However, the reported results evaluate representation-based pCR discrimination, calibration, context dependence, and concurrent-interval response encoding. No held-out next-visit latent/geometry error, future-image fidelity, or specified-action successor forecast result establishes L1 or L2. Permuted context is not L3 regime comparison. Decision curves are not L4 model-coupled optimization. No evaluated future latent/image forecast establishes L1/L2; pCR and contemporaneous state probes remain representation evidence.

scope.limits: Patient-disjoint held-out design stated; complete pretraining/statistic isolation audit not reported.
Separate trial cohort; no site count, formal overlap audit, external probability-calibration analysis, or prospective deployment established.

gate_assessments.rationale: Named clinical sources, patient-disjoint folds, causal-prefix masking, T0-centered preprocessing, and validation-only model/threshold/calibrator selection are reported. Complete isolation of all pretraining samples, treatment-category response standardization, target-construction statistics, and normalization fitting is not explicitly audited. Exact geometry definitions, missing-visit handling, and availability-time semantics are insufficiently reported. This prevents a complete evidence pass but is not proof of leakage.

Persistent observed-history state and executed learned next-visit transitions are documented, but reported endpoint/probe results do not establish held-out successor-state fidelity. A next-state training objective cannot substitute for rollout.one_step_evaluated. G02 is considered because a temporal world-model claim is made, although it is not a baseline gate of the selected representation profile.

The reviewed use predicts pCR from successively observed prefixes. It does not query an implemented multitime future-trajectory service. Multiple one-step training targets, four actual visits, and three observed-prefix evaluations are not multistep rollout horizons. No effective forecast horizon is assigned.

Actual held-out event-probability calibration is reported, including validation-only Platt scaling, Brier score, reliability diagnostics, and uncertainty. No prespecified use-specific calibration tolerance or acceptance policy is provided. These results do not establish latent-state uncertainty decomposition, external calibration, or joint-trajectory coverage.

Assigned-treatment categories explicitly condition the implemented transition, and endpoint AUROC responds to condition permutations. Dose, route, timing, duration, bundle-update semantics, and action support are insufficiently specified. No specified-action successor forecast result or matched clinically specified alternative-regimen consequence comparison satisfies the evaluation-stage requirements.

For the scoped predictive/context-dependence interpretation, the authors explicitly disclaim identifying treatment effects or estimating unassigned-regimen outcomes. A future therapeutic-effect interpretation would activate this gate and require new estimand, identification, assumptions, support, and validation evidence; none is inferred here.

The documented executed pipeline ends in a frozen-state logistic endpoint predictor and retrospective diagnostic analyses. There is no model-coupled action optimizer or learned decision policy. Training AdamW, logistic regularization search, and decision-curve thresholds are not treatment planning.

This assessment is restricted to offline retrospective representation/prediction research with no actual care-changing output or operational referral. The clinical-action release gate is therefore outside this use. Safety mechanisms themselves are not declared absent or irrelevant to any future clinical use.

A separate actual trial cohort and source-only transfer are evaluated, and receptor subgroups are examined internally. External discrimination declines with longer prefixes; the dual-task comparator is numerically stronger at T0–T1. Formal overlap controls, full acquisition/subgroup shift characterization, external calibration, and a use-specific acceptance criterion are not reported. R3 evidence does not automatically pass this stronger gate.

The reviewed claim is retrospective pCR representation/prediction, not human usability, expert preference, or sim-to-real policy utility. Clinical-trial participants supplying historical data are not a reader study of model outputs. Human-output evaluation remains not_reported rather than being fabricated.

No live workflow or patient-benefit claim is supported in the scoped results; authors explicitly limit decision curves to exploratory retrospective utility. Potential future treatment adaptation is not an executed prospective utility study.

No operational clinical release is documented. A promise of future research-code release does not constitute product authorization, monitoring, or a deployed intended-use dossier. Regulatory and lifecycle reporting remains unestablished for any future deployment.

This synthesis read all supplied text pages and all supplied visual-review notes. Original PDF bytes and page images were not directly accessible in this pass; image-inspection coverage is inherited as documented review provenance, not falsely claimed as a fresh visual examination.
Source hash, source path, and PDF availability are supplied metadata; the hash was not recomputed and disk existence was not checked.
No external bibliographic lookup, repository access, code inspection, experiment execution, file saving, or executable JSON-Schema/KG validation was performed.
Feature assertions are deliberately empty as requested. This is not a completed 128-feature annotation or an admission-ready graph package.
The supplied ontology excerpt names the feature catalog but does not include its complete per-feature definitions. No claim of executing a full feature-criterion validator is made.

An executed learned next-visit transition is documented, but no held-out next-latent, next-geometry, future-image, or free-running trajectory fidelity results are reported. Demonstrated capability is L0, not the legacy L2.

The T0-to-T2 shrinkage probe includes actual T2 in its representation and targets a response quantity explicitly used in pretraining. It is neither an unseen-future forecast nor independent biomarker discovery.
Response-state indexing differs among III-A, III-F, and Figure 1, including the baseline-only readout. Exact implementation needs clarification.

Patient-level folds and validation-only selection are stated, but every pretraining, preprocessing-statistic, treatment-category standardization, and target-construction operation is not explicitly audited for partition isolation.

Exact nine geometry features, response-vector dimension and construction, scalar response-score formula, contrastive similarity rule, physical voxel spacing, localization-fallback frequency, missing-visit/covariate handling, and detailed cohort exclusions are insufficiently reported.
Only ordered visit embeddings are specified. Clinical durations, regular cadence, action timing, dose, route, duration, concurrent regimens, and bundle-update semantics are not established.
Causal masking is temporal information control, not treatment-effect identification. The authors explicitly disclaim causal effects and unassigned-regimen estimation.

Treatment has no positive marginal AUROC increment in the cumulative ablation; its permutation effect tests fitted-model dependence under correlated treatment/subtype structure, not treatment efficacy.

Internal native fold means, pooled native subgroup results, pooled calibrated results, external averaged predictions, and permutation results must remain separate. Table IV aggregation and small Table I/permutation discrepancies are queued.

Cross-cohort I-SPY1 evidence is real retrospective external prediction, but discrimination declines with added visits; external superiority, probability calibration, prospective use, and benefit are not established.
The 791-patient shrinkage subset differs from the 808-patient cohort without a reported selection explanation.
Calibration is evaluated for final-pCR event probabilities, not latent-state uncertainty or joint trajectories. No use-specific acceptance tolerance or external calibration guarantee is supplied.
Decision-curve benefit is retrospective and threshold-dependent. It does not establish actual treatment adaptation, an evaluated action policy, or patient/workflow benefit.
No actual reader study, clinician-output evaluation, shadow deployment, prospective system intervention, comparative effectiveness, authorization, or post-release monitoring is reported.
Cumulative ablations use one addition order and a common seed; component interactions and multiseed robustness are not established.
Subtype pairwise nonsignificance does not establish equivalence or fairness; the TNBC longitudinal-gain result is exploratory and not multiplicity-corrected.
Bootstrap replicate counts, some statistical-test details, calibration-bin/ECE implementation, and several confidence intervals are not reported.
Some apparent numerical differences have explicitly different estimands or plausible rounding explanations. They are retained rather than silently corrected.
Model parameter count, hardware/runtime, inference latency, operational safeguards, security evaluation, detailed release licensing, and model weights are not reported.
Code is promised upon publication, not established as released. No cited system's capabilities or original-study validation is inherited.
Author-stated limitations include weak image-only discrimination with limited longitudinal data, reliance on handcrafted geometry, and the need for larger and more diverse external cohorts.
